feedback: This is the first iteration, so there is no earlier race outcome or telemetry to cite. What I had to set in the controller: the sensor row spans only 0.08 m against a 25 mm tape, so I scaled the weights to x*50 (range -2 to 2) so the signal is about 50 times the lateral offset, and I kept kp moderate (4.5) to avoid overshoot from a signal that can jump quickly when an outer sensor reads the tape. I used last_direction line-loss recovery because a loss most likely happens at the edge of a bend. The forward offset of 0.03 m gives the controller lead, and kd=0.25 was needed to damp that lead. If the next race shows completion on the oval with line_loss_events of 0 or 1 and low rms_error, keep the sensor span and forward offset and only tune the drivetrain. If the race shows line losses on the slalom or the s-bend, with readings dropping to near zero at the outer sensors, widen the sensor span (for example x = ±0.05 or ±0.06) before changing the controller. If the race shows the robot finishes on the oval but finishes slowly or hits the time limit, raise the wheel_radius or lower mass to get more speed for the same base_speed.
requested_changes: Widen the sensor span to x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 (keep y = 0.03) only if the next race shows line_loss_events above 1 on the slalom or s-bend, since iteration 0 has no evidence on saturation yet.
Reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg and keep wheel_track at 0.12 m, only if the next race shows completion_time above 2.5 s on the oval, since faster acceleration would be needed to finish within 3 s.
Move the sensor row forward to y = 0.05 m only if steering_oscillation is high on the oval, which would indicate the robot is reacting too late; keep y = 0.03 otherwise.
